title: The Book of Ezra Timeline
sub: Cyrus's Decree · the Hand of the LORD Was on Him
desc: Exiled Jews return to Jerusalem under a pagan king's decree to rebuild the temple, facing opposition, delay, and eventual completion, before a scribe named Ezra arrives to confront the community's compromise with intermarriage.

eras.label: Era One · Ezra 1
eras.name: Cyrus's Decree — the LORD Stirs Up a Persian King
eras.dates: Seventy years after Jerusalem's fall, a pagan king issues the decree that makes the return from exile possible, fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy

events.title: The LORD Stirred Up King Cyrus: Fulfilling the Word of Jeremiah
events.detail: In fulfillment of Jeremiah's prophecy, the LORD moves the Persian King Cyrus to issue a decree permitting the exiled Jews to return and rebuild the temple, even returning the sacred vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem.

verses.text: “In the first year of King Cyrus of Persia, in fulfillment of the LORD's [Yahweh's] message spoken through Jeremiah, the LORD [Yahweh] motivated King Cyrus of Persia to issue a proclamation.”

eras.label: Era Two · Ezra 2
eras.name: The Register of Returning Exiles
eras.dates: A detailed census of nearly 50,000 returnees, family by family, documents exactly who came back to rebuild Jerusalem

events.title: The Register of Those Who Returned: 42,360 Strong
events.detail: A detailed census records the families, priests, Levites, and temple servants who returned from Babylon under Zerubbabel, including those who could not prove their genealogy and were excluded from the priesthood until the matter could be settled.

eras.label: Era Three · Ezra 3
eras.name: The Altar Rebuilt — Weeping and Shouting Together
eras.dates: Worship resumes on the temple's original foundation before the building itself has even begun, producing an unforgettable mixture of grief and joy

events.title: The Altar Rebuilt: Burnt Offerings Resume Despite Fear of the Local Peoples
events.detail: Despite fear of the surrounding peoples, the returned exiles rebuild the altar on its original foundation and resume the daily burnt offerings, restoring worship before the temple building itself is even started.

verses.text: “They established the altar on its foundations, even though they were in terror of the local peoples, and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD.”

events.title: The Foundation Laid: Weeping and Shouting Mixed Together
events.detail: When the temple's foundation is laid, the priests and Levites praise the LORD antiphonally as at David's original dedication, but older people who remembered the first temple weep so loudly that the sound of joy and the sound of grief become indistinguishable.

verses.text: “People were unable to tell the difference between the sound of joyous shouting and the sound of the people's weeping, for the people were shouting so loudly that the sound was heard a long way off.”

eras.label: Era Four · Ezra 4
eras.name: Opposition Halts the Work
eras.dates: Local adversaries first offer false help, then resort to political sabotage that successfully stops construction for over a decade

events.title: The Work Came to a Halt Until the Reign of Darius
events.detail: After their offer to help build is rejected, local adversaries hire advisers to frustrate the project and eventually persuade the Persian king to order the work stopped entirely, halting construction for years until Darius's reign.

verses.text: “The work on the temple of God in Jerusalem came to a halt. It remained halted until the second year of the reign of King Darius of Persia.”

eras.label: Era Five · Ezra 5
eras.name: Prophets Stir the Work Back Into Motion
eras.dates: Two prophets reignite the stalled project, prompting fresh scrutiny from a new Persian governor

events.title: Haggai and Zechariah Prophesy: Work Resumes Under Scrutiny
events.detail: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah prompt the returned exiles to resume the stalled temple project; a new provincial governor questions their authority but allows the work to continue while writing to King Darius for confirmation.

verses.text: “God was watching over the elders of Judah, and they were not stopped until a report could be dispatched to Darius.”

eras.label: Era Six · Ezra 6
eras.name: Darius Confirms Cyrus's Decree — the Temple Completed
eras.dates: A search of the royal archives vindicates the builders, and the long-delayed temple is finally finished and dedicated with joy

events.title: Cyrus's Original Decree Found: Darius Orders the Work Funded
events.detail: A search of the royal archives uncovers Cyrus's original decree, and King Darius not only confirms it but orders the project funded from the royal treasury itself, with severe penalties for anyone who interferes.

verses.text: “The complete costs are to be given to these men so that there may be no interruption of the work.”

events.title: The Temple Completed: Dedicated With Joy and Passover Observed
events.detail: The temple is finally finished and dedicated with abundant sacrifices, and the returned exiles celebrate Passover together, rejoicing that the LORD had turned even a foreign king's heart to help them.

verses.text: “They sang, praising and glorifying the LORD [Yahweh]: ‘For he is good; his loyal love toward Israel is forever.’”

eras.label: Era Seven · Ezra 7
eras.name: Ezra Arrives — the Hand of the LORD Was on Him
eras.dates: Decades after the temple's completion, a second wave of return begins with a scribe devoted to studying, observing, and teaching the law

events.title: Ezra, Skilled in the Law, Comes to Jerusalem With Royal Authority
events.detail: Ezra, a scribe descended from Aaron himself and devoted to studying, observing, and teaching the law, arrives in Jerusalem carrying a sweeping letter of authority and financial support from King Artaxerxes, crediting it all to the good hand of God on him.

verses.text: “Ezra was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses which the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel had given… the hand of the LORD [Yahweh] his God [Elohim] was on him.”
“Ezra had dedicated himself to the study of the law of the LORD [Yahweh], to its observance, and to teaching its statutes and judgments in Israel.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Ezra 8
eras.name: The Journey to Jerusalem — Fasting Instead of Requesting a Guard
eras.dates: Rather than request royal protection, Ezra leads his caravan of returnees in fasting and prayer for a safe journey through dangerous territory

events.title: I Was Embarrassed to Request Soldiers: We Fasted Instead
events.detail: Having told the king that the LORD's protection rests on those who seek him, Ezra declines to request a military escort out of embarrassment, instead calling the whole company to fast and pray for safety on the dangerous journey, and they arrive safely with all their treasure accounted for.

verses.text: “I was embarrassed to request soldiers and horsemen from the king to protect us… So we fasted and prayed to our God about this, and he answered us.”

eras.label: Era Nine · Ezra 9
eras.name: Ezra's Prayer of Devastation Over Intermarriage
eras.dates: News of widespread intermarriage with idolatrous neighboring peoples drives Ezra to public grief and a prayer of collective confession

events.title: Our Guilt Has Climbed Higher Than Our Heads: a Prayer of Devastation
events.detail: Learning that the people, including leaders and priests, have intermarried with idolatrous local peoples in direct violation of the law, Ezra tears his clothes in public grief and prays an extended confession, marveling that God has shown any mercy at all to a people who keep repeating the same sin.

verses.text: “We are slaves, our God [Elohim] has not abandoned us in our servitude. He has extended kindness to us in the sight of the kings of Persia.”
“O LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel, you are righteous, for we are left as a remnant this day.”

eras.label: Era Ten · Ezra 10
eras.name: The Covenant to Send Away Foreign Wives
eras.dates: The book closes with a difficult communal decision and a detailed record of every family affected by it

events.title: Let Us Enact a Covenant to Send Away These Wives
events.detail: Moved by Ezra's public grief, the assembled people propose a covenant to separate from their foreign wives in accordance with the law, and a three-day assembly in the rain formally commits the nation to carrying it out.

verses.text: “Give praise to the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of your fathers, and do his will. Separate yourselves from the local residents and from these foreign wives.”

events.title: A Detailed List of Every Family Affected
events.detail: The book closes not with a triumphant summary but with a plain, unglamorous list naming every priest, Levite, and Israelite family involved in the intermarriage, down to the guilt offerings some of them brought.

verses.text: “All these had taken foreign wives, and some of them also had children by these women.”
